subject: Anthropic Renderer Rewrite ⚡, Claude CV Agent Tool 📄, Pi Coding Agent
intro: Anthropic shipped two quiet but telling updates: a smoother streaming renderer and enterprise-managed auth for MCP connectors. Neither is a model breakthrough. Both are pure infrastructure polish . That's the signal. The best AI labs now compete on feel, not just capability. Fixing re-render loops and OAuth friction is unglamorous work, but it's what separates a demo from a daily driver. Meanwhile, VoroTracing just beat Gaussian Splatting by 2.8x at 623 FPS. The rendering stack is getting a serious upgrade.

news.headline: Claude's streaming renderer rebuilt to run 4x smoother on long replies
news.body: You know that annoying freeze when Claude is typing out a long answer and your laptop just... chokes? Anthropic just fixed that. The old renderer had a simple but painful problem: every time a new word arrived, it would re-render the entire response from scratch. The longer the reply, the worse it got. Your CPU was doing way more work than needed. The new renderer is smarter. It only updates the parts of the text that are still actively changing. That one change unlocks some real numbers: This is live now on Claude web and desktop. No setup needed. Just open Claude and your next long response will feel noticeably smoother, especially on older or lower-powered machines.
bullets: Long replies stall 9x less on a slower laptop
On a 120Hz MacBook, it holds a steady 120fps the whole time

news.headline: Open-source Claude tool auto-writes your CV and cover letter for every job
news.body: Someone built a tool that applies to jobs for you. And it actually worked. Mads Lorentzen, a geophysicist, lost his job and built this framework to run his own search. 69 tailored applications, 20 first interviews, one signed contract. Then he open-sourced it. The clever part is the architecture: a drafter-reviewer pattern where two AI agents treat job applications as adversarial documents, not form-fill exercises. Think of it like a writer and an editor working together, automatically. Here is what it does for you: To get started: fork the repo, install Claude Code, Python 3.10+, and Bun, then run /setup and /scrape. It is a force multiplier, not an autopilot.
bullets: Evaluates job postings, tailors your CV, writes cover letters, and preps you for interviews.
You drop your CV and documents into a folder, and Claude reads and cross-references them before building your profile.
If you are outside Denmark, you can generate a search skill for your local job board using /add-portal.

news.headline: Pi's coding agent cuts context costs 88% by spilling tool output to disk
news.body: Most coding agents are just a while loop with a model and a few tools. Fine for 10 minutes. Run it for 50 hours and things fall apart. Pi's dev notes called out exactly why, starting with how other agents handle memory. When a tool spits out a huge log, agents like DeepSeek Harness trim it: keep the start, keep the end, delete the middle. Forever. If the actual error lived in that middle chunk, the model can never recover it . Pi's fix: prune + spill . Full output saves to disk. Context just holds a file path. The model greps it back when needed. Across 19 real sessions, this cut context usage by 26-35% and reduced processing costs by up to 88%. That last point matters. Model plus harness is becoming one unit. Evaluating a model alone is losing meaning fast.
bullets: Tool outputs spill to disk, never deleted
Intent logs before acting, result after, so crashes are recoverable
Claude behaves differently outside Claude Code because it was trained on Claude Code's specific tool shapes
